items.prose: Six lines from a student's CV.

rows: Built a bond pricer in Python; matched 50 quoted prices to 1p
Cut the society's budget overrun from £600 to £0 in one term
Tutored 6 GCSE maths students; 5 rose two grades
SQL: queried 3 million rows for a dissertation dataset

items.question: Tap the one line an interviewer could not test.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the line with no fact or number.

byKey.r0: That line has a tool and a number: 50 prices to 1p.
byKey.r2: That line has a before and an after in pounds.
byKey.r3: A predicted grade and an average are checkable facts.
byKey.r4: Six students and five results is testable.
byKey.r5: A tool, a size and a purpose: testable.

explain.text: "Excellent communication skills" is a claim with nothing behind it. Every other line gives a number, a tool or a result to ask about. Show communication with a line like the tutoring one instead (l6).

options.text: Tested if a 5-day reversal survives costs on 8 years of UK shares; net Sharpe 0.2, gross 0.7
Reversal signal project: Python, pandas, statsmodels, scikit-learn
options.why: You picked a tool list. It has no question and no result.

options.text: Innovative reversal research with strong, promising results
options.why: You picked adjectives. "Strong" gives no number to check.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Look for the question and the numbers (l7).

explain.text: The first entry states the question, the data and the result, gross and net. An interviewer can ask about every part of it. The others give tools or adjectives (l7).

items.question: A firm asks for a 90-second project account. Keep the same shares as the 2-minute budget: 15, 30, 45 and 30 seconds of 120. How many seconds go to the result?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Scale 45 seconds by 90/120.

byKey.same: You kept 45 seconds. The whole account shrank to 90, so every part shrinks.
byKey.sub: You took 30 seconds off the result alone. Every part shrinks by the same factor.

explain.text: The result is $45/120 = 37.5\%$ of the account. $37.5\% \times 90 = 33.75$ seconds; as a check, $45 \times 0.75 = 33.75$. At 130 words a minute that is about 73 words.

items.question: Which sentence makes the strongest start to a "why us" answer?

options.text: "At your October campus talk, a researcher showed how the firm tests signals on held-out years."
"You are the most respected firm in the industry."
options.why: You opened with flattery. It fits any firm and says nothing true and specific.

options.text: "Your values of curiosity and excellence inspire me."
options.why: You quoted the careers page back. The interviewer learns nothing new.

options.text: "Your interns are among the best paid in London."
options.why: You led with pay. It sounds like you would leave for more.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the fact you could name a source for (l8).

explain.text: The first sentence is specific, true and sourced: a talk, a month, a method. It sets up the link to your own evidence and the role (l8). Flattery, copied values and pay fit any firm.

items.question: Four options, +1 for right and −1 for wrong. You rule out one option and guess among the other three. What is the guess worth on average? Give three decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Right with chance 1/3, wrong with chance 2/3.

byKey.blind: That is a blind guess with four left. You ruled one out, so three remain.
byKey.nopen: You counted only the right answers. Wrong ones cost a mark.
byKey.zero: Zero needs two ruled out. With one ruled out, a guess still loses.

explain.text: $\tfrac13 \times 1 + \tfrac23 \times (-1) = -\tfrac13 \approx -0.333$. As a check, $2p - 1$ with $p = \tfrac13$ gives $-\tfrac13$. A guess breaks even only with two ruled out (l9).

items.question: Say a number-sequence test gives 15 items in 25 minutes. How many seconds is that per item?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Turn 25 minutes into seconds, then divide.

byKey.min: That is in minutes. Give seconds.

explain.text: $25 \times 60 = 1500$ seconds, and $1500 / 15 = 100$. As a check, $25/15 \approx 1.67$ minutes, and $1.67 \times 60 \approx 100$ seconds.

items.prose: A recorded answer to "Tell us about a challenge you faced", one sentence a line.

lines: Hi, and thanks for watching this.
Challenges are a big part of any degree, I think.
In my first year I failed a probability exam with 38%.
I changed how I studied: a timed past paper every week.
Now I start every module with its past papers.
params.title: Recorded answer

items.question: Tap the first line that answers the question.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the first line about a real challenge.

byKey.l2: Line 2 talks about challenges in general, not this one.
byKey.l4: Line 4 is what she did next. The story started a line earlier.

explain.text: Line 3 names the challenge with a number, so the answer starts there. Lines 1 and 2 are warm-up that a reviewer may skip (l10). Better still, make line 3 the first sentence.

items.question: Your best of 150 settings had an in-sample Sharpe of 1.9. Held out, it was 0.3. What does the CV entry lead with?

options.text: "Held out: Sharpe 0.3, from the best of 150 settings (1.9 in sample)"

options.why: You led with the in-sample best. "Out of how many?" sinks it at once.
You removed the result. The questions are the point; prepare for them.

options.text: "Sharpe about 1.1", the average of the two
options.why: You averaged two numbers that mean different things. Neither is reported honestly.

feedback.correct: The held-out number, with the trial count.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Lead with the number you can defend (l7).

explain.text: The best of many tries is high even with no edge, so 1.9 alone is misleading. The held-out 0.3, with 150 settings named, is honest and defensible. Backtesting Engine's Trials line makes the same point (l7).

items.prose: A firm allows no retake within 8 months (l4). On 20 November 2026 you sit its summer 2027 test unprepared and fail. Summer 2028 postings open about 1 July 2027.
items.question: What does the fail mean for summer 2028?

options.text: You are blocked until 20 July 2027, about three weeks into the summer 2028 window
It does not matter; summer 2028 is a new cycle
options.why: You assumed each cycle resets. The rule counts months, not cycles.

options.text: You are free again from 20 March 2027
options.why: You counted 4 months. The rule is 8.
You used 12 months. This firm's rule is 8.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count 8 months from 20 November.

explain.text: Twenty November 2026 plus 8 months is 20 July 2027. Summer 2028 postings open about 1 July, and early applicants are reviewed first (l3). So an unprepared sitting now costs the first weeks of the next cycle too.
